name: Inkjection FR
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading. The heading names the
network these frames are cut FOR and the channel is the show they are
cut from, so another show cutting for the same network is one more
folder under it rather than a heading of its own.
Like every channel under this heading it is a frame fetcher rather
than a thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of
vertical stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said
over it.
It is cut to Hall of Femme's design, and that pack is the one to read
first: the frame fetch, the vertical output, the transcription, the
rewrite, the block at the foot of the frame and every number in it
are the same and are named here rather than restated. What makes this
show itself is one sentence long - it is set in Texturina, on a card,
in a navy, a white and a red the user pairs per frame - and everything
below is that sentence.
The FR in the name is the account's, the way the DE in Hall of Femme
DE is and the FR in Soccer Stories FR: it says which of the brand's
feeds this is and not what language the app is in. What lands on the
frames is whatever the video's own voice track was saying, put
through the transcription and the rewrite exactly as on every channel
here; nothing in this pack changes that, and everything the app
itself says is English like the rest of it (see CLAUDE.md).
One thing this pack checked that most of its siblings had no reason
to, and that the two DE feeds checked before it. Both Texturina files
carry 634 codepoints and cover what French actually needs - the acute
and the grave, the circumflex on all five vowels, the cedilla, the
diaeresis, the o-e ligature, and the angle quotes French sets speech
in - so a caption is drawn from the file rather than from whatever
the browser substitutes for a missing glyph, which would be a
different face at a width nothing measured. Worth stating because a
face chosen for how it looks in English is not automatically a face
that can SET another language, and the check is two minutes against a
cmap.
A folder of its own rather than a second colourway of Hall of Femme,
for the reason oh-my-goal-news is a folder of its own: the person
picking a channel at the top of the app picks this one or that one
and never both, and these two do not merely disagree about colour -
they are set in different type, which is as far as two packs under
one heading go.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: What separates this show from the others under the heading: it is set
in Texturina Regular, with a picked word in Texturina Bold, in a navy,
a white or a red the user pairs per frame, on a card.
Everything else - the size, where the lines break, the capitals,
where the block stands on the frame, what picking a word covers, the
shape of the card - is the Snapchat caption design and is stated
once, in content/presets/snapchat-caption.json. This pack states only
what makes it this show.
The face is the brand and the ground used to be what made it
difficult. A serif at caption size over a still nobody chose the
contrast of is the hardest thing this app asks of a typeface: the
hairlines that make it a serif are exactly the strokes a photograph
eats. The file is the 18pt optical cut for that reason - the drawing
of Texturina made for reading, whose thins have some body to them
(see texturina-18pt-regular.json) - and it is still the right cut.
This show used to set its caption straight on the photograph, held
off it by a white halo, and wrote down that the day it wanted more
than one colour the remedy was a card. It asked for a white and a red
alongside its navy, for the letters and for a ground behind them, so
it is now on the card its carded siblings use. What follows from that
is written once, in content/README.md, under 'A channel that set its
caption on the photograph may take the card back'.

_comment_color: The dark navy, and the channel's own answer: what every frame is
set in until somebody presses a swatch, since a frame stores no
colour of its own until it is given one (see
state.textColorFor). It opens the list in `colors` below, so the
navy swatch is the one shown as chosen on an untouched frame.
Navy and not black, and that is still the brand rather than
decoration: a navy this deep is unmistakably dark at a glance, and
carries a colour the eye can name once it looks - which is what
makes the caption belong to a show rather than to the player.
_comment_colors: The show's navy, then the white and the red it asked for, offered
for the letters and for the card behind them - three buttons each
The same three in both lists and in one order, which is what every
carded pack under this heading does and for their reason: the
point is the PAIRING. Navy on white is what the show opens on;
white on red and red on navy are a button away.
Nothing stops the user setting navy on navy. The two lists are
independent because the pairing is the feature, and the user can
see the caption has gone and presses another swatch.
`text` reaches the highlight as well as the block - see the note on
`colors` in js/channels.js. The highlight here is a different CUT
of the face and not a different colour, so what colour the type is
has one answer and not two.
_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Texturina Bold, in the same navy as the
rest of the block. The highlight here is WEIGHT, which is Hall of
Femme's answer rather than Laugh Society's: one family, two cuts,
the change of voice being a change of volume and nothing else.
400 against 700 is the ordinary text pairing, and it is the right
one for this face - Texturina's Bold is drawn as the emphasis its
own Regular takes, and the two set on one line at the same cap
height with about five percent between their widths (both
measured in texturina-18pt-bold.json). That the cap heights are
identical matters on a card as much as it did on the photograph: a
picked word riding even slightly high would be visible against the
slab's edge as a fault in the sentence rather than as emphasis in
it.
The colour it names is the block's, so the recolour draws exactly
what its neighbours are drawn in and the weight is the whole of
the difference. Stated all the same, for the reason `color` above
is stated - a highlight that changed colour as well as weight
would be two highlights.
No shadow of its own any more. The white halo it used to restate
was there to match the block's on the photograph; with the card
back, the preset's null is right for both (see content/README.md).
The mode and the scope come from the preset, which is where the
argument for picking out words rather than lines lives.
_comment_panel: White, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are
the Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
White because it is the first colour the show asked for and the
navy reads on it at once - it is the ground the old white halo was
trying to give each letter, given to the whole line instead. The
red is the other card a button away.

_comment_branding: No dark gradient, like every carded pack under this heading: the
title is on a card and not on the photograph, so a ramp baked into
the picture has nothing to do. It would have worked against this
show's navy before the card came back, and it has nothing to work
No `scrim` either, for the same sentence.
